A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LSAS research work. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–F are readable and support comparison despite substantial experimental and presentation revisions.

before.justification: V4 reports original synthetic experiments, Cattaneo2 causal-effect estimates, and appendix studies of pretreatment-assumption violations and latent-variable counts.

after.justification: V5 reports original experiments on random graphs, specific causal structures, four benchmark networks, and Cattaneo2, including results for the added LDP comparator.

M1.justification: The TC discovery and R1/R2 search framework remains. However, Algorithm 1 changes from adding each estimate to Θ in v4 to assigning Θ ← θ in v5. Algorithm 2 also includes X among candidates when discovering Y’s Markov blanket. These are limited changes to the stated procedure; the MMB-to-MB renaming itself is cosmetic.

E1.justification: V5 adds Erdős–Rényi random-graph data and broadens benchmark evaluation to randomly selected treatment–outcome pairs that may have descendants. The specific structures, four named networks, and Cattaneo2 remain. Pretreatment violations were already evaluated in v4, but only through a narrower MILDEW study.

E2.justification: V5 replaces pretreatment adjustment (PA) with LDP in the synthetic and Cattaneo2 comparisons. LV-IDA with RFCI, EHS, and CEELS remain comparators. This is a focused membership update introducing a local method that relaxes the pretreatment assumption.

E3.justification: Simulation coefficients change from Uniform([-1,-0.5] ∪ [0.5,1]) to Uniform([0.5,1.5]), and sample sizes change from 2K/5K/7K/10K to 1K/5K/10K/15K. Fixed benchmark treatment–outcome pairs and latent selections are replaced by random selections, with revised latent counts. The new random-graph protocol uses 20–50 nodes, average degree 3, and 10% hidden nodes.

E4.justification: V4’s dedicated MILDEW latent-count sweep (Appendix E.2, Table 11) is removed. Its separate pretreatment-violation study (Table 10) is replaced by broader benchmark experiments allowing descendants, without retaining the earlier explicit comparison against pretreatment-respecting results. V5 also adds evidence about performance as random-graph size varies.

E5.justification: V4’s synthetic tables report averages with ± quantities for RE and nTest. V5’s corresponding simulation plots show averaged curves without error bars or dispersion estimates. Both versions still state 100 repetitions and retain 95% confidence intervals for Cattaneo2, but simulation uncertainty reporting is substantially reduced.

E6.justification: V5 replaces much of the synthetic RE/nTest evidence and adds random-graph and LDP results in Figures 4, 10, and 11. These use revised settings and do not establish same-setting performance gains. The new plots include cases where LDP uses fewer tests than LSAS. Cattaneo2 newly reports 266 tests for LDP, while CEELS’s 1284 and LSAS’s 158 remain unchanged; PA results disappear.

T1.justification: The five main theorems remain, but Appendix D.2 adds justification for joining paths that share nodes, and D.4 corrects a dependence statement to independence in Case 1. Separately, v5 Figure 9(b) adds X→Y, absent from v4 Figure 8(b), changing the S3 counterexample and removing its displayed graph without a causal effect.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction’s contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: local covariate selection with latent variables, soundness and completeness under the stated assumptions, and empirical accuracy and efficiency. The expanded experiments support these existing claims.

C2.justification: V5 attributes CEELS and LDP’s limited improvement with sample size to incompleteness and discusses performance when benchmark pairs may violate pretreatment assumptions. V4’s interpretation that increasing latent-variable counts has little impact disappears with that study. Appendix F adds multiple-environment data as a possible route to identification while retaining the principal limitations.

D1.justification: Reported hardware changes from 2.90/2.89 GHz Intel CPUs with 128 GB memory to a 3.60 GHz Intel CPU with 64 GB. V5 specifies standard Gaussian noise and adds an LDP implementation link. The earlier explicit two-hour runtime cutoff is no longer documented. Both versions continue to describe source code as included in supplementary materials.

R1.justification: V5 adds discussion of Maasch et al.’s LDP and LD3, distinguishing their assumptions and identification targets from LSAS. It also adds references for random graphs, earlier local structural learning, and identification across environments, while removing Rubin (1974) with PA. The overall positioning around complete local versus global adjustment-set discovery remains.

P1.justification: V5 standardizes MMB/AMMB to MB/AMB, refines theorem wording and explanations, condenses pseudocode, consolidates synthetic experiments into Section 4.1, and adds appendix contents. The main section sequence and much of the narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one. Causal diagrams and the real-data chart are redrawn, most synthetic-result tables become multipanel plots, and a random-graph results figure is added. The algorithm-complexity table moves from the main text to Appendix C.3. These substantially change the presentation beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: V5 improves experimental breadth and comparator relevance through random graphs and LDP, and strengthens parts of the proofs. However, removing simulation dispersion reporting and the dedicated latent-count study reduces empirical transparency. Adding X→Y to Figure 9(b) also weakens the S3 illustration by eliminating its displayed no-effect alternative. These material gains and losses do not support a reliable net judgment of overall improvement.
